policies: I judged each query by asking whether a session that issued it would want the memory back, not by vocabulary overlap: several memories use a query's exact words while answering a different question (e.g. keyword-spelling memories against a case-folding query), and several answer without sharing any word (the cold-start centroid observation against a query about small stores). Multi-topic queries -- whether joined by 'and' or by commas -- were read as unions, so a query naming dirty flags, per-target bases and the drop/restore safety copy collects everything on each leg rather than only memories spanning all three; the same for the Golden Rule query and the traversal query. Bare-noun queries ('attribution', 'reconciliation', 'store registry design') were read as topic sweeps and labelled generously across the topic's core mechanics, with adjacent-but-derived material pushed to borderline. A bare identifier ('MemoryView') was read as a request for the memory that decides that thing, not for everything the thing touches. Where a query was readable two ways I took the reading the wording most directly supports and then let borderline carry the other reading's material rather than merging them. The relevant/borderline line: relevant means the memory states, decides, or measures something the query asks for, and I would defend it in a review; borderline means the memory is one hop away -- it supplies the mechanism a relevant memory uses, applies the same rule to a neighbouring field, records a consequence of the answer, or is the same shape of problem in a different subsystem. Memories that merely share a keyword with the query and answer nothing it asked went in neither list.

queries.q: how are similarity scores computed across memory sets
queries.reading: Read as: how is a similarity score made comparable when a query searches several stores at once. Relevant is the union-centroid machinery and the same-model precondition; the general centroid decision and single-store cosine mechanics sit borderline because they do not address the cross-set part.

queries.q: what happens to similarity scores in a store with very few memories
queries.reading: Read as: what does the scoring do when the corpus is tiny. The observed one-memory-scores-zero case answers it directly; the centroid decision, the small-corpus caveat on local scaling, and the cold-start threshold note are borderline because they bear on it without being about few memories.

queries.q: lone vector is its own centroid so a single memory scores 0.0
queries.reading: Read as a statement of the cold-start artifact, wanting both the observation and the mechanism that produces it. The observation and the mean-subtraction decision are relevant; union-centroid and threshold memories are borderline as the same arithmetic in a different setting.

queries.q: MemoryView
queries.reading: Read as a bare type name: the memory that decided a single shared view type carries a memory's complete field set to every tool. Kept narrow -- memories that merely describe what recall returns are borderline, not answers about the type itself.

queries.q: how case folding of keywords works
queries.reading: Read as: what does the system do about keyword case. Only the spelling convention actually states the folded-form-beside-the-written-form arrangement; the set-name rule (explicitly not case-folded) and the spelling-drift memory are borderline as the adjacent cases a reader would also want.

queries.q: how are keyword lookups made case-insensitive without altering what was stored
queries.reading: Same subject as the previous query with the design constraint spelled out; the separate-column answer is the one memory that satisfies both halves. The set-name rule is borderline because it is the deliberate counter-case, not an answer.

queries.q: mutation testing
queries.reading: Read as: where does this project use mutation testing. Relevant are the four memories that record a mutation as the thing holding a guard, or that classify the mutation script as a development-only tool. Left borderline empty: memories about tests in general are not about mutation testing.

queries.q: dirty flag, reconciliation base per target, drop and restore safety copy
queries.reading: Three named topics, labelled as a union: the dirty flag and its removal from the destructive path; the reconciliation base keyed by record and target; and the unconditional safety copy on drop and restore. Base-migration and store-registry consequences are borderline -- they follow from the per-target base rather than describing it.

queries.q: why the convention catalog is deliberately kept small
queries.reading: Read as: what is the reasoning for the small catalog. Relevant are the scope-limiting decision, the context-cost framing, the character budget and its raises, and the built-in inclusion criterion. Memories that merely invoke the constraint while deciding something else are borderline.

queries.q: two servers disagreeing about the embedding model
queries.reading: Read as the two-server model-mismatch problem: the observed loop, the oscillation analysis, and every rule written to answer it. Single-process embedding-state memories (mixture, provenance, blocked writes) are borderline because they describe the condition rather than the disagreement.

queries.q: reconciliation base migration
queries.reading: Read narrowly as the migration of stored reconciliation bases. Relevant are the never-keep-what-you-cannot-prove rule, the never-merge-across-targets rule, the canonicalisation route, the cost of dropping, the urgency assessment, and the false-base invariant that motivates all of them. Base definition and the designs that would obsolete the per-target base are borderline.

queries.q: attribution
queries.reading: Bare-noun topic sweep over who a memory and a store are attributed to: store author, per-memory created-by/modified-by, claiming, correction and re-attribution, plus origin as human-versus-LLM. Tombstone attribution and the export gate's last-modifier scoping are borderline -- attribution appears there in service of another decision.

queries.q: reconciliation
queries.reading: Bare-noun topic sweep over store-against-file reconciliation: the two reconciliations, the base, the decision table, checksum comparison, tombstones changing what absence means, the anomaly, and the ordering hazard. Base migration, git-side file merging, and the import/restore split are borderline as neighbouring layers.

queries.q: store registry design
queries.reading: Read as a sweep of the store-registry proposal: what the registry holds, identity versus location, placement and discovery, registration, status reporting, inspect, and the costs and consequences. Trust/set-name questions the registry would answer, and the per-target base it would remove, are borderline.

queries.q: store registry in-tree
queries.reading: Read as the specific question of putting the store inside the repository tree. Relevant are the memory that rules in-tree out and the proposal that places stores centrally instead; the other placement memories (home versus common directory, the reserved directory's contents) are borderline because they answer where among out-of-tree locations.

queries.q: how keywords should be chosen and spelled when storing a memory
queries.reading: Read as the keyword-writing convention: how many, how spelled, whether to coin or reuse, the reserved prefix, and the rejected person-name ban. Keyword use elsewhere -- embedding input, keyword search, set-declared conventions -- is borderline because it is about what keywords do, not how to pick them.

queries.q: the Golden Rule, memories about people, charitable judgement versus accurate technical criticism
queries.reading: Union of three legs: the Golden Rule itself and its four demands, memories that characterise people, and the charity-versus-accuracy boundary. All three legs live in one body of reasoning, so the relevant list is large by construction. The misuse-friction memory and the reinforcement-channel memories are borderline.

queries.q: tombstones, forgotten memories, counting records in a set versus live memories
queries.reading: Union of tombstones, forgetting, and the record-count-versus-live-memory distinction. The first two legs are well covered; the third has no memory that states it directly, so status memory counts and the graph-shape measurement sit borderline rather than being stretched into relevant.

queries.q: near-duplicate detection before storing, surfacing neighbours versus warning, similarity thresholds
queries.reading: Union of pre-store duplicate checking, the surface-neighbours-rather-than-warn decision, and thresholds. Relevant are the half-overlap argument, the threshold-avoidance argument, the recall-before-storing convention and the twins evidence. Confidence anchors, cold-start separation and the general affordance rule are borderline.

queries.q: a convention that names an operation the catalog does not define, withholding convention text until tools exist
queries.reading: Read as the withholding rule: convention text drafted before the tools it names exist, and held back until they do. The correcting-convention case and the written-but-unserved-is-normal note answer it; catalog adjacency, pointing-versus-restating, and the which-half-first argument are borderline.

queries.q: confidence field calibration, what a low confidence number means, recalibration versus a new belief
queries.reading: Union of confidence calibration, what a low value means, and recalibration versus supersession. Relevant are the ladder and its measurement, the anchors-not-thresholds rule, the laundering hazard at the low end, both recalibration-is-an-amendment memories, the claim/apparatus split, and the low-confidence reading of a sweeping characterisation.

queries.q: served convention text read by strangers, examples that assert facts about the reader's own store
queries.reading: Read as the drafting rule for served text: it is read by strangers, so an example asserting facts about the drafter's own store is false for its reader. Relevant are that test, the state-don't-derive rule, the reinforcement-versus-comment split, and the routing draft that compiled one user's arrangement into everyone's catalog.

queries.q: malformed tool call remark, warning rather than refusing, surfacing damage in the response
queries.reading: Union of three: refusing a malformed call in a way the caller can act on, preferring a directive warning to a refusal, and reporting damage in the response rather than silently. Reporting decisions in adjacent subsystems (status, forward-compatibility, tripwires) are borderline.

queries.q: graph traversal from seed memories, link labels, decay by distance, fan-out
queries.reading: Union of four: the walk from seeds, the link-label vocabulary, decay with distance, and fan-out bounds. Labelled as one body because the traversal design and the label vocabulary are each asked for by name. Reverse-index mechanics, link-target structure and per-label open questions are borderline -- they concern edges without concerning the walk.
